summary: Likasi, Haut-Katanga's second city and a copper/cobalt mining and rail hub, is firmly state-held and far from the eastern conflict zones. Daily order in its communes and health-area neighbourhoods is kept by the PNC, with FARDC garrisons in the city; provincial authorities imposed a night curfew on Lubumbashi and Likasi in February 2025 and police-army anti-banditry operations (e.g. Operation Ndobo) continued into 2026. Urban banditry and armed robbery are significant but no gang or militia holds territory. Bakata Katanga militia activity in 2025-2026 is reported in remote areas (e.g. Mitwaba/Upemba, Luisha sector ~67 km away), not in Likasi. Peri-urban villages (Kampemba, Buluo) have no reported armed-group activity and are assessed as default PNC presence.

sources.title: Le gouverneur Jacques Kyabula prolonge le couvre-feu à Lubumbashi et Likasi pour 15 jours
Lubumbashi - 7 présumés bandits et deux femmes arrêtés dans le cadre de l'opération Ndobo
Double attaque meurtrière à Luisha : l'IGM alerte sur la montée de l'insécurité dans les zones minières
Haut-Katanga : face à la recrudescence de l'insécurité urbaine, la police lance l'alerte

zones.description: Likasi city: all communes and health-area neighbourhoods (Kikula health zone)
zones.evidence: Likasi is under normal state administration; PNC policing with FARDC support, including curfew enforcement (Feb 2025) and joint anti-banditry operations into 2026. Urban banditry is reported but no non-state group controls any neighbourhood; Bakata Katanga activity is in remote areas, not the city.

zones.description: Peri-urban villages in Likasi city limits: Kampemba 1/2, Kampemba (Kakontwe HA), Buluo (Panda/Kambove health zones)
zones.evidence: No reported armed-group activity in these villages adjoining Likasi; nearest reported 2026 armed attack was in Luisha sector ~67 km away. Assessed as default state (PNC) presence.
